headline: Approved art gallery at 131 Leeder Hill Drive, Unit 7 with conditions; released $26,925.75 bond at 20 Davis Street.
summary: The Ely Center for Contemporary Art proposed turning an industrial condo unit into a gallery. The site plans 113 parking spaces, with 46 for the gallery, but 126 were required, and staff said the commission can reduce that requirement. Commissioners also issued a favorable report on a plant donation and adopted the 2027 meeting schedule.
decisions: Approved the special permit and site plan for an art gallery at 131 Leeder Hill Drive, Unit 7, with conditions, unanimously.
Approved the release of the $26,925.75 bond for 20 Davis Street, unanimously.
Issued a favorable report, unanimously, on the donation of native plants to Eli’s Garden of Healing.
Approved the October 13, 2026 regular meeting minutes as written; Commissioner Bauer abstained.
Adopted the proposed 2027 regular meeting schedule, unanimously.

Meeting Minutes 
 
Hamden Government Center 
2750 Dixwell Avenue 
Hamden, CT  06518 
Tel: (203) 287-7070 
Fax: (203) 287-7075 
 
November 17, 2026 
The Planning and Zoning Commission, Town of Hamden, held a hybrid Public Hearing and Regular 
Meeting on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. The meeting was held in-person in the Legislative Council 
Chambers at Hamden Memorial Town Hall , 2372 Whitney Avenue, Hamden, CT 06518, and remote ly 
via Town Zoom teleconferencing at https://www.hamden.zoom.us/j/82468227728.  
 
Commissioners in Attendance: 
 
In Person: Michele Mastropetre (Chairman), Joseph McDonagh 
(Vice Chairman), Richard Pearce, Hannah Leckman, 
Barbara Andrews, Felicia Bond, Richard Bauer, Ronald 
Leonardo, Calvin DeMarsilis 
  Staff in Attendance: In Person: Eugene Livshits (Town Planner), Christopher Soto 
(Assistant Town Planner), Maisie Albis (Commission 
Clerk), Tim Lee (Assistant Town Attorney) 
Via Zoom: Genevieve Bertolini (Stenographer) 
  
Chairman Mastropetre called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. The clerk read the agenda into the 
record, and Commissioners and staff introduced themselves.  
 
A. Public Comment Session 
  Chairman Mastropetre called for comments from the public regarding topics within the purview 
of the Commission. None of the remote or in-person attendees wished to speak. The Chairman closed 
the public comment session.  
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
B. Public Hearing 
 
1. Special Permit and Site Plan #26-1405 
131 Leeder Hill Drive, Unit 7 
Art Gallery/Exhibition Space 
Applicant: The Ely Center for Contemporary Art 
Daniel Burns, a member of the board of the Ely Center for Contemporary Art, presented the 
application. He was joined by other members of the board, including Claire Nardi, John 
O’Donnell, Adrian Bergstrom, and Aaron Pine, as well as Gallery Director Amy Burg. Mr. Burns 
explained that the Center is currently located in Fair Haven but is seeking a permanent space. The 
application proposes the conversion of an industrial condominium unit to an art gallery space.
Page 2 of 5 Planning and Zoning Commission 11.10.26 Minutes 
 
Mr. Burns said that the Center sees about 5-10 patrons each day at its current location, with 
closer to 20 visiting on weekend days. He reported that parking calculations done by Godfrey 
Hoffman Hodge, LLC suggest that 46 spaces would be sufficient for the use.  
Chairman Mastropetre asked if the gallery space was for viewing only or for artists to sell 
their work. Ms. Burg explained that it would be up to the individual artist whether or not to sell 
the pieces they choose to display. Commissioner Pearce inquired about the types of art on display, 
which Ms. Burg said could vary widely but has included painting, sculpture, photography, 
performance art, and collage.  
In response to a question from Commissioner DeMarsilis, Ms. Burg reiterated that the Center 
typically sees low foot traffic. She said that the current location is open to the public on 
Wednesdays, Thursdays, and Sundays and typically sees a maximum of 10 visitors each day. 
Commissioner DeMarsilis then asked about special events, which Ms. Burg said were infrequent 
and typically attracted a maximum of around 75 patrons over the course of an event. Ms. Burg 
confirmed to Commissioner Bond that the space would be used exclusively by the Center and its 
resident artists and would not be made available for rent by outside parties. 
Commissioner McDonagh asked how many full-time staff members would be present on site. 
Ms. Burg replied that she would be the only staff.  
Chairman Mastropetre then requested that Mr. Livshits read his report. In it, he reviewed the 
proposal for compliance with the zoning regulations. He highlighted the fact that the applicant 
was proposing 113 parking spaces, with 46 dedicated to the art gallery/exhibition space, though 
126 spaces were required per Table 5.5. He explained that the Commission has the authority to 
modify the parking requirements if an applicant can demonstrate that less parking would be 
sufficient. Mr. Livshits suggested that the applicant’s statement of use demonstrated that the 
Center would have limited foot traffic and its operating hours would be complementary to 
existing uses, thus supporting a reduced parking requirement. His report concluded with the 
recommendation that the Commission approve the application subject to the following 
conditions: 
1. A change of use permit must be submitted prior to opening 
2. Submittal of house of operation for the Art Gallery and Exhibition Space 
3. Signage will require a separate zoning permit. 
Commissioner Pearce clarified whether Mr. Livshits was recommending that the Commission 
modify the requirement in this case and asked why they would choose to go against their own 
regulation. Mr. Livshits explained that the regulation itself granted the Commission discretion 
when warranted. Commissioner DeMarsilis was similarly concerned about setting a precedent for 
future applicants. Mr. Lee advised that the regulation indeed granted discretion to vary the 
standard and that the application should be evaluated on its particular merits without 
consideration to precedent. 
Chairman Mastropetre then opened the floor to comments from the public. In-person 
attendees Adriana Bergstrom, Alex Valentine, Christian Miller, and Andrew Argres spoke in favor
Page 3 of 5 Planning and Zoning Commission 11.10.26 Minutes 
 
of the application. They expressed excitement about the prospective center and the benefits they 
feel it will bring to the community. No online attendees made any comments and there were no 
in-person comments opposing the application.  
The Chairman reported the receipt of a written comment of support from Suzan Shuten, 
which was signed by Mario Almeida, Joy Bush, Kim and Kevin Van Aelst, Sheldon and Louise 
Krevit, Joan Fitzsimmons, Alan Neider, Howard el Yasin, Branden Biggs, Susan Sternberg, Hank 
Paper, Nicole Pollard, and Karen Dow. The Chairman also noted that the RWA reviewed the 
application and had no comment. She then closed the public hearing for the item. 
 
C. Regular Meeting 
 1. Special Permit and Site Plan #26-1405 
131 Leeder Hill Drive, Unit 7 
Art Gallery/Exhibition Space 
 Applicant: The Ely Center for Contemporary Art 
Commissioner McDonagh moved to approve the application subject to the conditions 
listed in Mr. Livshits’ report, as follow: 
4. A change of use permit must be submitted prior to opening 
5. Submittal of house of operation for the Art Gallery and Exhibition Space 
6. Signage will require a separate zoning permit. 
Commissioner Bauer seconded and all were in favor. The application was unanimously 
approved with conditions. 
 
2. Bond Release—Zoning Permit #27043 
20 Davis Street 
Bond release request: $26,925.75 
Applicant: Pat Munger Construction Co. Inc. 
Mr. Soto referred to his memo to explain that the sedimentation and erosion control bond had 
been held during construction work at the Hamden Hall Country Day School, and that the 
conditions for release had been met. Commissioner Bond moved to approve the bond release 
request. Commissioner McDonagh seconded and all were in favor. The request to release 
the $26,925.75 bond was approved unanimously. 
 
3. C.G.S. §8-24 Review #26-453 
Donation of Native Plants to Eli’s Garden of Healing 
Applicant: Town of Hamden 
Mr. Livshits read his staff report outlining the referral. The Connecticut Audubon Society is 
prepared to donate native plants to create a bird habitat at Eli’s Garden of Healing in DeNicola 
Park, he said. Chairman Mastropetre asked if there were requirements for what species were 
planted. Mr. Soto replied that the donation plants would be native species but that there were no
Page 4 of 5 Planning and Zoning Commission 11.10.26 Minutes 
 
further requirements.  
Commissioner Bauer raised a concern about planting occurring in the cold months and asked 
whether it should be done in the springtime. Chairman Mastropetre advised that the fall season 
was appropriate for planting anything with a bulb.  
With no further questions, the Chairman called for a motion. Commissioner McDonagh 
moved to issue a favorable report to the Legislative Council. Commissioner Bauer seconded 
and all were in favor. A favorable report was issued unanimously. 
 
 D. Old Business 
 
 
 
1. Review of October 13, 2026, Regular Meeting Minutes 
Chairman Mastropetre called for any necessary corrections to the minutes; there were none. 
Commissioner Bauer announced that he would be abstaining from a vote as he had not been 
present at the meeting. Commissioner Leckman moved to approve the minutes as written. 
Commissioner McDonagh seconded. Commissioner Bauer abstained and all others voted in 
favor. The minutes were approved as written. 
   
E. New Business 
 
 
 
 
      
 1. Review of Proposed 2027 Regular Meeting Schedule 
Chairman Mastropetre asked staff if the proposed schedule had been checked against major 
holidays, which they confirmed. She then called for a motion. Commissioner McDonagh moved 
to approve the proposed 2027 Regular Meeting schedule. Commissioner Bauer seconded 
and all were in favor. The schedule was adopted as proposed. 
 
2. Upcoming Town Center Master Plan Design Workshop 
Mr. Livshits informed the Commission of an upcoming design workshop and open house for 
the Town Center Master Plan project. The event will be in Thornton Wilder Hall at Miller 
Memorial Library on November 18, 2026. The workshop will run from 5:30-6:30 p.m. and the 
open house from 6:30-7:30 p.m. He said that the consultants on the plan will be presenting 
conceptual designs, and that the event will be a good opportunity for Hamden residents to provide 
their input.  
 
F. Adjournment  
 Commissioner DeMarsilis moved to adjourn. Commissioner Bond seconded and all were in 
favor. Chairman Mastropetre adjourned the meeting at 7:48 p.m.  
 
 Submitted By: ______________________________ 
Maisie Albis, Commission Clerk
